caption:
This morning: an architect tested 13 AI models, and Claude Opus 5.5 produced a drawing set he judges good enough for a building permit.

The deep dive: Codersera lists $5.98 per completed task for Opus 5.5, vs $5.86 for Opus 5. NOT CONFIRMED: we could not find this figure on the cited page. Also listed: 5.4x GPT-6 Sol's cost per evaluation task, and 86.3 out of 100 on BenchLM, ranked #2 of 216.

My take: cheaper tokens are not a cheaper result. Measure cost per finished, checked task.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: The morning post said an architect tested 13 models, and Opus 5.5 produced a drawing set he judges permit-quality. I went back in to check the numbers around it.
First, Codersera lists $5.98 per completed task for Opus 5.5 against $5.86 for Opus 5, but we could not confirm it on their page.
Second, MindStudio's comparison puts Opus 5.5 at 5.4 times GPT-6 Sol's cost per evaluation task, with token prices double.
Third, BenchLM scores Opus 5.5 at 86.3 out of 100, second of 216 models. Strong, but a general score, not drafting.
Cheaper tokens may not mean a cheaper result. If you use Opus 5.5, what do you pay per finished task? Comment CHECK and tell me.
